analysis.title: Agentic AI Driving ~30% of 2030E CPU Units, >$200B CPU TAM Ahead, Memory Tailwinds
key_insights: Mizuho estimates agentic AI at ~4% of server CPU demand in 2026E, rising to ~30% by 2030E. Server CPU TAM goes from ~$68B in 2026E to ~$209B in 2030E (32% 4Y CAGR), with agentic CPUs reaching ~$80B (123% 4Y CAGR).
Segment split of the 2030E server CPU TAM: agentic ~$80B, head-node ~$68B (~61% 4Y CAGR), traditional ~$60B (~2% 4Y CAGR). The ~$209B total sits below AMD's own target of >$220B.

Demand evidence cited: META's Muse passed 5M downloads in 22 days (vs 56 days for ChatGPT, 103 for Grok, 493 for Claude). OAI reported >1.2B weekly active users at DevDay and launched 'Dots', always-on agents that run tasks 24/7.

Bottom-up model: agentic-enabled MAU grows at a 51% 4Y CAGR to ~4.2T by 2030E, and agentic tasks per user per day reach 21.5K (86% CAGR). Agentic CPU deployments grow at a 92% 4Y CAGR from 1.1M in 2026E to 14.6M in 2030E.
NVDA is seen as having the steepest server CPU ramp, from ~$7B to ~$60B, overtaking AMD and INTC by 2027E as Vera ramps. AMD and INTC grow from ~$12B/$17B in 2025 to ~$44B/$41B by 2028E.

ARM is expected to become a merchant CPU player in 2027E with its AGI CPU, with >$2B of orders already secured. It also earns royalties on Vera, Cobalt, Graviton and Axion as CSPs ramp in-house CPUs. Mizuho sees ARM gaining CPU share from x86.
DELL CPU-only server revenue is seen growing from ~$19B in 2025 to ~$40B by 2028E, and SMCI from $7B to $17B, driven by agentic orchestration demand and traditional enterprise servers.

Token consumption is growing >4x y/y into 2H26E, and agentic AI may need 5-30x more tokens per task than a standard chat query. Token pricing is down >50% since mid-2026E, and CSPs are pushing efficiency through prompt caching, routing to smaller models and latent-reasoning architectures.
Memory: agentic AI is modeled at 22-30% of server CPU, DRAM and NAND bits shipped by 2030E, including ~22% of NAND demand (the SNDK discussion cites 22%, the summary cites 18%).
PT changes: AMD to $705 from $580, INTC to $114 from $92, DELL to $650 from $600, SMCI to $43 from $35, SNDK to $2,050 from $1,875. Ratings are unchanged.

INTC is Neutral. Mizuho expects it to be lifted by sector CPU multiple expansion but to underperform peers. It is positive on INTC server CPU ramps and potential foundry wins (TPU on EMIB-T in 2028E), while Diamond Rapids may launch in 2027E with potential delays.

Agentic CPU comparison: ARM AGI CPU (136 cores, 300W, best cores/watt but supply-limited), AMD Venice (256 cores, 1,024MB cache, 600W), NVDA Vera (88 cores, 450W, per-core bandwidth, suited to latency-sensitive agents), INTC Diamond Rapids (256 cores, 1.28GB cache, launch 2027E).

market_movers.rationale: PT raised from $580 to ~41x F27E P/E (prior ~34x). C26/C27E EPS is seen growing ~87%/123% y/y on agentic server CPU demand, Venice ramping and MI450 ramping at OAI and META in 2H26E. Bull case $900, bear case $550.
PT raised from $92 to ~8x F27E P/S (prior ~6x) on multiple expansion across CPU peers. Mizuho sees INTC underperforming peers. Bull case $145, bear case $83.
PT raised from $600 to ~18x F28E EPS (prior 17x). F27/28E EPS is seen up 148%/38% y/y, with an AI server backlog of $95B and Vera-only racks potentially built by DELL. Bull case $850, bear case $500.
PT raised from $35 to ~8x F28E EPS (prior ~6x). Headwinds are orders shifting to competitors and pricing and financing pressure. F27/28E revenue is seen up 74%/11%. Bull case $55, bear case $31.

PT raised from $1,875 to ~9x F27E EPS vs SOX at 19x. GM is seen staying >80%, EPS growing 5x over F26-F28E, and a potential buyback of 25-30% of the company from $30-50B of FCF in 2027-28E. Bull case $2,600, bear case $1,600.
Key long-term beneficiary through the AGI CPU (2027E ramp) and royalties from Vera, Graviton, Axion and Cobalt. PT is ~2.5x F28E PEG. Bull case $700, bear case $150.
Fast inference leader. Mizuho sees agentic proliferation (>1000x token generation vs reasoning-only tokens) widening its advantage. PT is ~12x F28E P/S. Bull case $465, bear case $165.
Benefits from HBM share gains, memory pricing and agentic memory demand. PT is ~3x F28E P/B. Bull case $1,850, bear case $1,000.
Standalone CPU revenue is ~$20B and could grow >100% y/y in 2027E/F28E as Vera ramps. PT is ~20x F28E EPS. Bull case $450, bear case $185.

sector_views.rationale: Agentic AI is expanding server CPU TAM to >$200B by 2030E and lifting AMD, ARM, NVDA and INTC. Mizuho also sees demand for DRAM and NAND.
Agentic orchestration demand drives CPU-only server revenue at DELL and SMCI alongside AI server growth.
Agentic AI is modeled at 22-30% of server CPU, DRAM and NAND bits shipped by 2030E, supporting MU and SNDK.

earnings_insights: AMD: Mizuho estimates C26/C27E EPS growth of ~87%/123% y/y (estimate, not reported). The PT is based on ~41x F27E P/E.
DELL: Mizuho estimates F27/F28E EPS growth of 148%/38% y/y (estimates). The AI server backlog is $95B and the five-quarter pipeline is a multiple of the backlog.
SMCI: Mizuho estimates F27/28E revenue growth of 74%/11% and EPS growth of 35%/17% (estimates).
SNDK: Mizuho estimates EPS growing 5x from F26 to F28E (estimate), with GM >80% under NBM agreements.
NVDA: Mizuho estimates F27E CPU revenue of ~$20B, with F28E potentially up >100% y/y (estimates).
risk_factors: Agentic AI adoption, tasks per user and CPU penetration assumptions may not materialize at the modeled pace.
ARM AGI CPU supply may be limited by volume ramps. INTC Diamond Rapids may face delays in 2027E.
Token pricing has fallen >50% and CSPs are pushing efficiency measures, which could reduce compute demand per task.
Memory cost and supply tightness weigh on PC and server unit sales (DELL, INTC).
SMCI faces share loss, pricing pressure, financing and unresolved internal control issues.
Memory ASP declines and cyclicality, and a return to broad memory oversupply, are the main MU and SNDK risks.
Customer concentration: OpenAI is growing to >80% of CBRS revenue, SMCI's two major customers are ~58% of sales, and ARM's top 5 customers are >50% of revenue.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: META's Muse passes 5M downloads 22 days after launch (Sensor Tower).
Exhibit 5: Agentic AI share of global server CPU shipments rises from 4% in 2026 to 30% in 2030, DRAM from 4% to 30%, NAND from 2% to 22%.
vol_and_positioning: SNDK trades at ~9x F27E EPS vs the SOX C27E P/E of 19x, which Mizuho calls a big discount as peer multiples rise.
DELL at ~18x F28E EPS is slightly below the SOX at ~19x.
geopolitical: Escalating China export restrictions and Taiwan tensions are cited as NVDA risks, with NVDA shipments to China yet to resume after US re-approval.
Middle East entities G42 (UAE) and MBZUAI accounted for ~86% of CBRS 2025 revenue. Mizuho expects the mix to fall to <40% in F26E and <5% in F27E+ as OpenAI ramps.
Arm China and geopolitical headwinds are cited as ARM risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Agentic penetration of server CPUs rises from ~4% to ~30% by 2030E, taking the server CPU TAM to ~$209B and lifting AMD, NVDA, ARM and the memory makers.
tension_points.bear_case: Token pricing is down >50% and CSPs are pushing efficiency (prompt caching, smaller models), which could cut compute per task. The model also depends on agents being reliable enough to run most workflows on their own, and Mizuho notes possible overlap between head-node and agentic CPUs.
